sections.content:
Wait — the arm is still showing N at 29-32 and 35-38 (A@29 and C@35)! And the image shows A@29 selected (G ring) and C@35. So the catastrophe didn't happen!
What happened? I clicked (19,36) → selected C? Then clicked (19,30) → C's target is 23... but the arm still shows A@29 and C@35, and A is selected (G ring at 29 in the image).
Hmm! So clicking (19,36) selected C, and then clicking (19,30)... (19,30) is inside A@29's body (A spans columns 29-32)! So the second click didn't click C's target slot 23 — it clicked A's blob body → switched selection to A. That's why A is now selected.
I made a coordinate mistake: C's target slot is 23, and its center is around columns 23-26 → click (19,24). Earlier at T20 I clicked (19,24) to trigger the catastrophe. And A@29's body spans columns 29-32, so (19,30) is on top of A.
So current state: {A@29 selected, C@35}. Same as before. No catastrophe. Good — no damage done.
Now, to trigger the catastrophe: click (19,24) — but wait, is (19,24) inside A's body? A spans columns 29-32. 24 is not in that range. Slot 23 spans roughly columns 23-26 (the w pattern). (19,24) is empty (w) → clicking it while C is selected → C jumps to 23, crossing A@29 → catastrophe.
But wait — do I really want the catastrophe? Let me reconsider the plan. The decisive test requires the initial state. Alternative: is there a way to test landing on an occupied slot without the initial state? Landing on an occupied slot requires a blob's target to be occupied. Currently: A@29 (target = own position, no-op), C@35 (target 23 is empty, but crossing 29 = A → catastrophe). B is gone. So no.
OK, proceed with the catastrophe route:
1. Select C: MOUSE(19,36).
2. Click C's target (19,24) → catastrophe → key appears.
3. Find the key (the earlier scan only found S background — the key must be in a different location; the earlier scan region was rows 44-63, columns 0-31, all S. The key might be at columns 32-64, or rows <44. Let me scan the whole board for colors not in {B,W,w,c,S,N,g,G} — the key was probably Y or O or P. Actually, from the earlier catastrophe image (T16?), the key was at bottom-left... but the scan found nothing. Maybe the key is drawn in a color within my background set? Unlikely. Let me scan the entire bottom half for any color not in {S,B,W,w,c}.
4. Click the key → reset → verify initial state.
5. Select C (19,36), click target (19,24) → landing on B@23 → observe.
Let me execute steps 1-2 and the key scan.
